hold_text: This diff edits scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py and scripts/ops/claim_merge_slot.py — two of the 11 entries in LANDING_MACHINERY — so R12 refuses self-landing and a human merges. That is the right outcome: this changes what R13 will ACCEPT, which is exactly the kind of change that should not be able to wave itself through. ⚠️ AND IT CANNOT SELF-LAND IN A SECOND, STRONGER SENSE: the branch would have to ARM to exercise the new route, and arming a landing-machinery diff is what R12 forbids — so the route ships PROVEN IN A SANDBOX AND UNEXERCISED ON A REAL PR, and that is stated rather than glossed. WHAT A HUMAN IS BEING ASKED TO READ: R13 gains a SECOND way to be satisfied — a per-branch claim at .github/merge-slots/<slug>.json — alongside the existing shared session-board.json::merge_slot field, which is UNCHANGED and still passes. It only ADDS a way to satisfy R13; it removes none, and commit-to-main plus the 27 workflows behind it keep working byte-for-byte (asserted side by side in the self-test, both routes PASS). The per-branch route is not weaker: the branch is named INSIDE the file as well as in its path and the two must agree, added-or-modified is still required so an inherited claim is not an ask, and held_by/claimed_at are still mandatory. THE JUDGEMENT CALL IS WHETHER R13's SHARED FIELD WAS BUYING ANYTHING: R13's own docstring says it does NOT serialize — a committed claim reaches no other session until the branch merges — so the shared field bought a guaranteed conflict and no exclusion, and attribution is fully preserved. If you disagree with that reading, this is the PR to say so on.
why: MI-280, an INSERTED unit. IT ANSWERS AN ALREADY-FILED ROW AND THAT ROW IS NOW CITED, WHICH IT WAS NOT WHEN THIS PR WAS OPENED: BL-20260909-R13-FORCES-EVERY-ARMING-BRANCH-ONTO-ONE-SINGLE-HOLDER-KEY-SO-CONCURRENT-PRS-DIRTY-EACH-OTHER-BY-CONSTRUCTION. Its resolution_criteria has two clauses and this change addresses BOTH, but finishes only one -- say which. CLAUSE (1) asks for the RATE over a stated population, which the row says nobody has and which MI-275 could only offer as n=1: PAID IN FULL by the measurement below, plus the four-armed-vs-two-hold control. CLAUSE (2) asks for a mechanism under which two branches need not write the same lines at all -- exactly what the per-branch claim is, and exactly what MI-275's own update says a client-side merge driver does NOT deliver -- but it demands the mechanism be SHOWN by arming two branches concurrently, not by a green test, and this PR cannot do that because arming a LANDING_MACHINERY diff is what R12 forbids. So the row is UPDATED, not closed, and the demonstration is the first thing to do after this merges. The original framing follows — not one of U1..U7, and filed as one because it is an unforeseen blocker that must be resolved to release the rest, which the manager checklist explicitly treats as a first-class edit. Tier-1 tooling: scripts/ci/**, scripts/ops/**, .github/** and tests/** only; no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no order path. THE TIER IS NOT THE OBJECTION; the PATH is. THE DEFECT, MEASURED WITH A POPULATION AND TWO CONTROLS. merge_slot is ONE field in ONE file that every armed branch must overwrite, so every armed branch conflicts with main the moment anything else claims it. Population: the last 40 commits to main touching docs/claude/session-board.json (2026-09-11T23:12Z -> 2026-09-12T09:30Z). 39 of 40 MOVED merge_slot.branch — so it is not that the file is busy, it is that THAT FIELD is what moves. Inter-move gaps (n=38): min 3.3m, median 11.5m, max 61.8m, with 26 of 38 under 16 minutes and 17 of 38 under 10. Against that, one CI cycle. Resolving the conflict pushes a new head and RESTARTS CI, so resolving faster does not help — the clock restarts each time. THE CONTROLS: on 2026-09-12 one session held six open PRs; all FOUR armed ones went dirty together and the only TWO that stayed clean were the two declaring landing: hold, which write no claim at all. The claim is the one difference between them, measured twice about 15 minutes apart with the same result. AND THIS REPO ALREADY FIXED THIS EXACT CLASS ONCE, ONE LAYER OVER: .github/pr-automerge-request was a single shared file every requesting PR had to modify; it collided by construction, hit live 2026-08-21 (#10083 merged, #10086 came back mergeable_state dirty with that file as the ONLY conflicted path, costing a merge commit and a full CI cycle in a repo that has hit the free-tier minutes cap once), and was split into .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt. The R13 claim is the same defect in the same route and takes the same remedy. WHAT IS NOT GIVEN UP: nothing, because R13 never serialized — its own docstring says a committed claim reaches no other session until the branch merges, so two branches can each arm, each write a valid claim, and never see one another. Attribution and timestamping are preserved exactly and strengthened (the branch is named in the PATH and in the BODY, and both must agree — the filename alone is not the claim, since a file copied from another branch could be renamed). The coordination-board MERGE SLOT CLAIM comment is untouched and remains the authoritative live claim. VERIFICATION, INCLUDING TWO ESCAPES THAT WERE FOUND AND CLOSED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER. Guard self-test: 7 positive controls hold and all 21 planted defects fail, up from 19 — including a NEW POSITIVE control asserting an armed branch passes on the per-branch claim while NOT touching the shared field, which is the property the whole change exists to buy. Source mutations against the new predicates: 7 of 7 caught, positive control quiet on restore. ⚠️ ON THE FIRST RUN ONLY 5 OF 7 WERE CAUGHT. Deleting the added-or-modified check ESCAPED, because every existing plant writes a file ABSENT on base, so that branch was never reached; and accepting a valid-JSON NON-OBJECT escaped, because the 'not valid JSON' plant fails at json.loads and never reaches the isinstance branch. BOTH ARE THE SAME SHAPE — a control that cannot reach the branch it targets, which is precisely how the scope-overlap parser sat broken behind a passing suite — and both now have plants, the first reproducing the real case by landing a claim on main and MERGING it in rather than simulating it. 27 existing pytest cases in test_claim_merge_slot.py and test_commit_to_main_callers.py still pass unmodified, and claim_merge_slot.py --self-test and check_automerge_trigger.py both still pass. PROVEN IN A SANDBOX, UNEXERCISED ON A REAL PR: the branch cannot arm to test the new route, because arming a landing-machinery diff is what R12 forbids. A live exercise is the first thing to look for after this merges.
